name: Fatty Acid Degradation Beta-Oxidation
notes: for a genome to have fatty acid degradation capability via beta-oxidation, it should encode at least one acyl-coa dehydrogenase (fade,k06445,k00249,k00255,k09479), one enoyl-coa hydratase (fadb,k13767,k01825), and thiolase (fada,k00632) completing one full ≈í‚â§-oxidation cycle.

name: Alkane Tranformation (Archaeal)
notes: for a genome to have anaerobic alkane transformation capability, it should encode for a methyl-com reductase catalytic subunit (mcra, k00399). encoding for other subunits (mcrabcdg, k00399,k00401,k00402,k00421,k00422) is detected. this annotation will identify canonical mcr and divergent mcr or mcr-like sequences mapping to the same ko, performing an mcra phylogeny is recommended. presence of an mcr without phylogenetic placement can suggest multiple different metabolisms falling under anaerobic alkane transformation capability (various forms of methanogenesis, reverse methanogenesis, anaerobic alkane degradation).

name: CO2 Fixation
notes: for a genome to have co‚Äö√á√á fixation capability via the acetyl-coa pathway, it should encode: the complete codh/acs complex (cdha, cdhb, cdhc, cdhd, and cdhe subunits), which together catalyze co‚Äö√á√á reduction to acetyl-coa. this is distinct from the wood-ljungdahl pathway row which additionally requires (eastern) methyl branch genes.

name: Wood-Ljungdahl Pathway
notes: for a genome to have wood-ljungdahl co2 fixation capability, it should encode the complete western brnach codh/acs complex for either the bacterial (k00198, k14138) or archaeal (k00192, k00195, k00193, k00194, k00197) and have at least one eastern/methyl branch entry point (fdha k01938 or fhs k05299). presence of both branches indicates full reductive acetyl-coa synthesis from co2 molecules.

name: 3-Hydroxypropionate/4-Hydroxybutyrate (3Hp/4Hb) Cycle
notes: for a genome to have 3hp/4hb co‚Äö√á√á fixation capability, it should encode all of the 3 following genes - 1) k14534, 2) either malonyl-coa reductase or acetyl-coa carboxylase (k15017, or k18603-5, respectively) 3) either k15039 and k18602) .presence of all three modules indicates complete autotrophic co‚Äö√á√á fixation via the 3hp/4hb cycle, something previously characteristic of crenarchaeota in marine sediments.

name: Calvin-Benson-Bassham (Cbb) Cycle
notes: for a genome to have cbb cycle co‚Äö√á√á fixation capability it should encode ribulose-bisphosphate carboxylase large chain (rbcl, k01601), phosphoribulokinase (prk, k00855), and one ribulose-phosphate 3-epimerase (rpe, k01783) to differentiate the cbb cycle from the rhp metabolic pathway.

name: Reductive Glycine Pathway
notes: for a genome to have reductive glycine pathway co‚Äö√á√á fixation capabilit, it should encode at least 3 proteins/subunuts of the glycine cleavage system (k00283, k00282, k02437, and k00605) and at least 5 of the glycine reductase  (k10671, k10672, k00384, k21577, k21576, k03671, and k10670).

name: Rtca Cycle
notes: for a genome to have reductive tca cycle it should encode either 1 atp-citrate lyase (k15233 or k15232) or citryl-coa synthetase+citryl-coa lyase (k15233 or k15232, and k15234).

name: Rump Pathway (Non-Methanogenic Methylotrophy Type I)
notes: for a genome to have rump pathway methylotrophy capability it should encode hps (k08093,k13831,k13812) and phi (k08094) a methanol dehydrogenase (mdh, k00093,k23995,k17066,k14028,k14029) and at least one  together these suggest capacity to convert methanol and formaledehyde into usable fructose 6-phosphate.

name: Serine Pathway (Non-Methanogenic Methylotrophy Type Ii)
notes: for a genome to have serine pathway methylotrophy capability it should encode serine-glyoxylate transaminase (sgt, k00830), hydroxypyruvate reductase (hpr, k00018), and malyl-coa lyase (mcl, k08691). additional encoding of serine hydroxymethyltransferase (shmt, k00600) further supports likelihood of having this pathway.

name: Hydrogenotrophic Methanogenesis
notes: for a genome to have hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis capability it should encode the mcr complex (mcrabg, k00399+k00401+k00402), the mtr complex core subunits (mtra-e+h, k00577-k00581+k00584; mtrf/g omitted due to less consistent annotations), at least 2 of the 4 upper c1 pathway steps (ftr-k00672, mch-k01499, mtd-k00319 or hmd-k13942, mer-k00320), and at least one fwd/fmd subunit (k00200-k00205). this combination distinguishes hydrogenotrophic methanogens from obligate methylotrophic lineages (which lack mtr) and from aceticlastic methanogens (which lack the upper c1 pathway). anme archaea encode the same genes in reverse so performing an mcra phylogeny is highly recommended to confirm methanogenesis direction. methylotrophs that also do hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis e.g. canonical methanosarcinales) will present as matched to this row and "methylotrophic and aceticlastic methanogenesis". distinguishing between methanogenesis pathways via gene presence/absence is not recommended for genomes less than 90% complete.

name: Methylotrophic Methanogenesis
notes: for a genome to have methylotrophic or aceticlastic methanogenesis capability it should encode the mcr complex (mcrabg, k00399+k00401+k00402) plus at least one substrate-specific entry point. i.e. methanol, methylamines, methylated sulfur, or acetate . for methanol potential enzymes are mtab (k04480), mtaa (k14080), or mtac (k14081); for methylamines potential enzymes are mtba (k14082), mtmb/monomethylamine methyltransferase (k16176), mtmc/monomethylamine corrinoid protein (k16177), mtbb/dimethylamine methyltransferase (k16178), mtbc/dimethylamine corrinoid protein (k16179), mttb/trimethylamine methyltransferase (k14083), or mttc/trimethylamine corrinoid protein (k14084); for methylated sulfur potential enzymes are mtsa (k16954) or mtsb (k16955); for acetate, enzymes are acka+pta (k00925+k00625) or acs (k01895), combined with codh/acs core subunits cdhc+cdhe+cdhd (k00193+k00197+k00194). here, aceticlastic methanogenesis overlaps with co2 fixation and wood-ljungdahl rows, but is distinguished with the presence of the mcr complex. performing an mcra phylogeny is recommended to distinguish between methanogenesis and anaerobic methanotrophy. distinguishing between methanogenesis pathways via gene presence/absence is not recommended for genomes less than 90% complete.

notes: the reduction of nitrous oxide (n‚Äö√á√áo) to dinitrogen gas (n‚Äö√á√á) is catalyzed by nitrous oxide reductase (nosz, k00376). presence of this gene indicates the potential for the final step of denitrification, converting n‚Äö√á√áo into n‚Äö√á√á.

name: NO3 To NO2
notes: nitrate reduction to nitrite can occur through either the membrane-bound nar system (k00370 and k00371, both required) or the periplasmic nap system (k02567 and k02568, both required). either system completes the nitrate transformation step.

name: DNRA
notes: dnra reduces nitrate to ammonium through a two-step process: nitrate reduction via nar or nap systems, followed by nitrite reduction via nrf or nir enzymes. presence of one nitrate reductase system and one nitrite reductase system indicates dnra capability.

name: NO2 To NO
notes: nitrite reduction to nitric oxide (no) is carried out by either nirs (k00368) or nirk (k15864). presence of either gene indicates capacity for nitrate/nitrite reduction in denitrification.

name: NO To N2O
notes: the conversion of nitric oxide (no) to nitrous oxide (n‚Äö√á√áo) is catalyzed by nitric oxide reductase, encoded by norb (k04561) in bacteria or cyp55 (k15877) in fungi. presence of either gene indicates the capacity to perform this denitrification step

name: Aerobic Nitrite Oxidation
notes: aerobic nitrate oxidation (nitrite oxidation) is the second step of nitrification, where nitrite is oxidized to nitrate by the nxr complex (nxrab) under oxic conditions, completing the conversion of reduced nitrogen to its most oxidized form.

name: Aerobic Ammonium Oxidation
notes: aerobic ammonium oxidation converts ammonia to nitrite through sequential reactions catalyzed by ammonia monooxygenase and hydroxylamine oxidoreductase. presence of one ammonia monooxygenase subunit set and hydroxylamine oxidoreductase indicates this capability.

name: N2 Fixation

name: Dissimilatory-Sulfate-Reduction
notes: Dissimilatory sulfate reduction to sulfide (H2S); key souring mechanism in oil & gas systems. Requires adenylysulfate reductase (aprAB; K00394, K00395) and dissimilatory sulfite reductase (dsrAB; dsrA, dsrB).

name: Thiosulfate-Reduction-(Respiratory)
notes: Respiratory thiosulfate reduction via the PhsABC thiosulfate reductase complex (phsA K08352, phsB K08353, phsC K08354). Requires at least 2 of 3 subunits to account for incomplete genome recovery in metagenomic data. Uses thiosulfate as terminal electron acceptor under anaerobic conditions. Found in Salmonella, Citrobacter, and diverse anaerobes.

name: Thiosulfate-Reduction-(Rhodanese)
notes: Thiosulfate sulfurtransferase (rhodanese; K01011 rdl/glpE-type, K14180 mitochondrial-type) transfers sulfur from thiosulfate to cyanide or other acceptors, producing sulfite and thiocyanate. Also involved in sulfur relay and cyanide detoxification. Distinct from respiratory thiosulfate reduction ‚Äö√Ñ√Æ does not conserve energy via electron transport. Extremely widespread across bacteria and archaea so interpret cautiously; presence alone is not diagnostic of dedicated thiosulfate metabolism.

name: Sulfur-Oxidation-Sox

SoxXA (K17223, K17222) initiate sulfur binding, SoxYZ (K17226, K17227) are the sulfur-carrying proteins, and SoxB (K17224) is the sulfate-releasing thiohydrolase. SoxCD (K17225, K22622) are optional and indicate complete oxidation to sulfate without intermediates.

name: Sulfur-Oxidation-Reverse-Dsr
notes: Oxidation of stored sulfur globules via reverse-running DsrAB, distinguished from reductive DsrAB by co-occurrence with dsrL (K27196), an NADH-dependent oxidoreductase found exclusively in sulfur-oxidizing organisms. Both dsrA/dsrB (K11180/K11181) and dsrL (K27196) required. Found in Chlorobi, some Gammaproteobacteria, and Chromatiales.

name: Tetrathionate-Reduction
notes: Tetrathionate reduction via the ttrABC system (ttrA K08359, ttrB K08358, ttrC K08357). At least 2 of 3 subunits required. Relevant as an alternative electron acceptor in anaerobic subsurface and industrial systems.
